newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: "Sleeping Beauty" prince kisses off Vienna shares.
newsitem.headline: "Sleeping Beauty" prince kisses off Vienna shares.

text.p: Jim Rogers, the U.S. investment guru who in 1985 saw in the Austrian stock market a sleeping beauty and kissed it to life, said on Tuesday he had largely sold off his Vienna shareholdings.
"I've still got money invested in Austria, but not much in shares, rather little," Rogers, former Quantum Fund manager with George Soros and author of "Investment Biker", told reporters.
Rogers said he withdrew from Austrian shares because the country lagged behind others in implementing structural changes to improve competitiveness.
Rogers is credited with kicking off the Vienna stock market bull runs in 1985 and 1989 with his recommendations.
In late trade on Tuesday, Vienna's blue-chip ATX index was trading at an all-time high, up more than one percent at 1,258.8 points. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12 256
